Part 2&3 地点 PLACE

Describe your favorite city that you have visited

描述你最喜欢的一座城市

⚠️ AI 范例，仅供学习 — IELTS 口语全程独立完成，背诵照搬 AI 答案会被考官识别为背稿。

Part 2 话题卡片

Describe your favorite city that you have visited

  • Where it is (它在哪里)
  • How you knew it (你怎么知道它的)
  • When you visited it (你什么时候去的)
  • And explain why it is your favourite city (并解释为什么它是你最喜欢的城市)

问题与答案

Cue CardDescribe your favorite city that you have visited

I'd like to describe Shenzhen, my home city, which sits right on the southern coast of China, just across the border from Hong Kong. I suppose you could say I've known it my whole life, because I was born there and I've lived there ever since, so it's not really a city I visited, more the city I grew up in. Actually, I still remember exploring different corners of it as a kid, and I keep discovering new parts of it even now. The thing is, when I think about why Shenzhen means so much to me, a few specific places come to mind. There's Qianhai, where you can walk along the sea and watch the sunset over the bay, and Shenzhen Bay Park, which is great for a relaxing weekend. I also love the area in Bao'an around Bay Glory, which has the tallest ferris wheel in Asia. And of course, the whole city is full of young people chasing opportunities, especially in tech, which gives it that energetic, prosperous feel. As a result, Shenzhen is my favourite city because it's incredibly convenient, modern and always moving forward. Honestly, with so many job opportunities and such a bustling atmosphere, I can't imagine living anywhere else. All in all, it's more than just a city to me. It's part of who I am.

我最喜欢的城市是深圳，南方沿海、毗邻香港；我出生在那里长大，前海、深圳湾公园和宝安摩天轮都难忘，生活便利、繁华又充满机会。

Q2Which is more suitable for young people, urban life or rural life, and which is more suitable for old people?

I'd say, generally speaking, urban life suits young people better, while rural life tends to suit older people more. For young people, cities offer jobs, education and a lively social scene, which they need at that stage of life. In my country, for instance, graduates flood into places like Shenzhen for opportunities. That said, it really depends on the individual, because some older people actually enjoy city life, and quite a few young people dream of a quiet countryside lifestyle.

总体说城市更适合年轻人（机会多、热闹），乡村更适合老人（安静）；但也要看个人性格。

Q3How do people choose a city to travel to?

Well, I think it's a mix of practical and emotional reasons. The main practical ones are budget, distance and time, since most people can't afford a long trip. But emotionally, people are drawn by food, famous sights and, these days, what they see on social media. For example, in my country, a popular series or a trendy photo spot can make a city suddenly famous overnight. Having said that, recommendations from friends probably carry the most weight.

人们选旅游城市看预算、距离等实际因素，也受美食、景点和社交媒体网红点影响，朋友推荐往往最关键。

Q4Do you think a tourist city is also a good place to live? Why?

Not necessarily, I'd say. A tourist city can be a wonderful place to live because the infrastructure is usually well developed, with good transport, restaurants and entertainment. However, there's a downside, because tourist crowds push up prices, and the streets can get uncomfortably busy during peak seasons. In my country, some coastal tourist towns struggle with that every summer. So on the whole, I think it depends on your tolerance for crowds and your budget, rather than the city itself being good or bad.

旅游城市基础设施好、吃喝玩乐多，适合居住；但游客多会推高物价、街道拥挤，是否宜居取决于个人承受力。

Q5Do most people prefer to travel in a modern city or a historical city?

I think it largely depends on the person's age and interests, but I'd say young people generally lean towards modern cities, whereas older travellers often prefer historical ones. Modern cities appeal because they offer shopping, nightlife and stunning skylines that look great in photos, like Shanghai or Shenzhen. Historical cities, on the other hand, attract people who want culture and heritage, like Xi'an. That said, more and more people now want a bit of both, mixing modern comfort with history in one trip.

大体上年轻人偏爱现代城市（购物、夜景、拍照好看），年长者偏爱历史古城；如今更多人想两者兼顾。

Q6Do you think big cities will continue to attract more people in the future?

I imagine they will, yes, at least in my country. The main reason is that big cities concentrate opportunities, like well-paid jobs and good universities, which small towns simply can't match. For example, Shenzhen grew from a small fishing village into a megacity in just a few decades. Having said that, if remote work keeps expanding, some people may choose cheaper, smaller cities, so the growth might slow down. But I doubt big cities will ever lose their appeal entirely.

大城市还会继续吸引人，因为机会集中；但如果远程办公普及，增速可能放缓，不过大城市不会失去吸引力。
